greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Here's your Sunday read, with a big week in AI and a tense one in Melbourne.

lead.headline: Anthropic starts trading on Nasdaq in a record-setting IPO
lead.summary: Anthropic listed on Nasdaq on 19 November, with shares priced at $83 and opening far higher in what reports call the largest IPO on record. Analysts are treating the stock as a proxy for the wider AI trade.

stories.headline: Cluster-based training set selection beats active learning for materials ML
stories.summary: Published in Nature Computational Science (18 Nov), the study benchmarks 100 algorithms across 60 chemistry and materials tasks and finds cluster-based selection of training data is the most data-efficient option in low-data settings. It is backed by a theoretical framework explaining why.

stories.headline: Photonic chips trained in place with physical gradient descent
stories.summary: A Nature Computational Science paper (INSPIRE) trains photonic neural networks directly on the chip by measuring gradients in the physical system, reporting large compression and training speed-ups. The journal also ran a research briefing on it; it was published in October but is still circulating.

stories.headline: AI-native laboratory runs autonomous biomolecular experiments
stories.summary: Nature published AutoDNA, an autonomous lab where AI agents plan and run multi-objective biomolecular experiments across different instruments. It drew news coverage as an example of AI-driven science.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with a 20% price cut
stories.summary: OpenAI released the two models on 17 November, pricing Astra at $8 per million input tokens, about 20% below its predecessor. It now matches Claude Fable 5.2 on price while trailing it slightly on one benchmark index.

stories.headline: Nvidia stops shipping H200 chips to China
stories.summary: On its 17 November earnings call, Nvidia's acting CEO said it has stopped shipping licensed Hopper data-center products to China. The company says the revenue impact will be small given strong demand for newer chips.

stories.headline: Eight US states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT and child safety
stories.summary: State attorneys general allege ChatGPT was marketed as safe while harming minors and misleading parents, seeking penalties and changes for young users. The suits were filed in mid-October and remain a live story.

stories.headline: Police investigate three separate stabbings across Melbourne
stories.summary: A 21-year-old man died after an alleged stabbing in the CBD, and three teenagers were arrested nearby. Two other men were seriously hurt in separate attacks, including one at Broadmeadows.

stories.headline: Man hospitalised after stabbing at Bourke Street Mall
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man suffered serious injuries in an attack in the heart of the CBD on Saturday.

stories.headline: Greens win injunction over Prahran how-to-vote cards
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has restrained distribution of how-to-vote cards in Prahran that the Greens argued were misleading, with the state election a week away on 28 November.

stories.headline: Latest Victoria news from ABC Melbourne
stories.summary: ABC's Victoria feed also covers the run-up to the state election, a reopened coroner's inquiry into a police officer's death and a Walk Against Family Violence.

stories.headline: Ukraine's strike collapses a road span of the Kerch Bridge
stories.summary: Drones and missiles destroyed a road section of the bridge linking Russia to Crimea, halting traffic while Russia promised repairs. Zelensky framed it as a response to attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure.

stories.headline: Iran steps up drone attacks on US targets in Bahrain
stories.summary: Bahrain said it intercepted a fresh wave of Iranian drones, which Tehran's Revolutionary Guard says targeted US military radar. The attacks are raising Gulf tensions.
